title.id: Perintah Kepailitan, Restrukturisasi dan Pembubaran (Kriteria dan Keadaan yang Ditetapkan menurut Pasal 72F dan 250F) 2021

completenessNote: 全文，共 5 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。

text.en: 1. This Order is the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution (Prescribed Criteria and Circumstances under Sections 72F and 250F) Order 2021 and comes into operation on 29 January 2021.

heading.en: Prescribed criterion under section 72F(2)(e) of Act

text.en:
2. For the purposes of section 72F(2)(e) of the Act, an additional eligibility criterion is that the company seeking to enter into the simplified debt restructuring programme is not a foreign company.
[S 26/2026 wef 29/01/2026]

heading.en: Prescribed circumstance under section 72F(3)(l) of Act

text.en:
3.—(1) For the purposes of section 72F(3)(l) of the Act, the circumstance mentioned in sub‑paragraph (2) is also a circumstance that makes a company unsuitable for entry into the simplified debt restructuring programme.
[S 26/2026 wef 29/01/2026]
(2) The circumstance is that a declaration or an injunction has been made or granted by the District Court or the General Division of the High Court against the company under section 9(1)(a) or (b) of the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (Cap. 52A).
[S 26/2026 wef 29/01/2026]

heading.en: Prescribed criterion under section 250F(2)(f) of Act

text.en:
4. For the purposes of section 250F(2)(f) of the Act, an additional eligibility criterion is that the company seeking to enter into the simplified winding up programme is not a foreign company.
[S 26/2026 wef 29/01/2026]

heading.en: Prescribed circumstance under section 250F(3)(m) of Act

text.en:
5.—(1) For the purposes of section 250F(3)(m) of the Act, the circumstance mentioned in sub‑paragraph (2) is also a circumstance that makes a company unsuitable for entry into the simplified winding up programme.
[S 26/2026 wef 29/01/2026]
(2) The circumstance is that a declaration or an injunction has been made or granted by the District Court or the General Division of the High Court against the company under section 9(1)(a) or (b) of the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act.
[S 26/2026 wef 29/01/2026]
